app.nav.sim_title: OrbitFlow runs on offline datasets in a digital twin; it is not connected to a satellite.
app.note.data_english: Interface translated. Data-derived text (agent rationales, event logs, document titles and quotations) is shown in English, exactly as the system produced or cited it.

app.hero.kicker: LEO beam hopping · ITU AI for Good
app.hero.lede: OrbitFlow forecasts demand, lets a learned policy point the beams, and has every decision checked before it runs.
app.hero.anim: Animation: a satellite moves a beam to a cell whose demand is rising, then the guard checks the decision
app.act.1.sub: Demand starts rising in one cell
app.act.2.sub: BRIDGE moves a beam there early
app.chase.h2: A fixed rotation drowns the busy cells. A greedy one forgets the quiet ones.
app.chase.lede: Same demand, three schedulers. Orange means data is waiting.
app.chase.late_simple: arrive late with a simple scheduler
app.chase.insight: The simple scheduler looks fast on average, but it forgets quiet areas: {a} of time-critical data arrives late. OrbitFlow keeps that to {b} at the same throughput. The price is more beam switching: {c} switches per slot against {e}.
app.fore.h2: Forecasting buys time only when demand gives a warning.
app.fore.lede: A gradual ramp can be seen early. A sudden jump cannot.
app.fore.ramp_sub: The forecast shown at each slot is its estimate for two slots later, made from lagged telemetry.
app.fore.skill: Error reduction at demand jumps, against repeat-last
app.fore.skill_sub: Held-out test episodes, MAE on targets more than 5 Mbps from the last observation.
app.fore.more: The forecaster is a small GRU neural network that predicts three 10 ms slots ahead from delayed measurements. Over all slots, including calm ones, it is no better than repeating the last value, and worse on bursty and block traffic. Its value is concentrated at ramps. A gradient-boosted baseline was also tested and lost on most scenarios.
app.fore.insight: A forecaster cannot see a hotspot that appears from nothing. It cut surge error by {a}, and by only {b} on the real pass.
app.loop.h2: The AI proposes. Everything else checks.
app.loop.lede: One loop, every 10 ms. Select any step.
app.flow.aria: Decision loop flowchart; select a step
app.node.telemetry.role: Demand, queues and channel state from the twin, one 10 ms slot old. Geometry and signalling timing are known exactly.
app.node.validator.role: Bad or stale reports get their last good value; too much bad data switches the slot to conservative mode.
app.node.forecaster.role: Predicts each cell three slots ahead. Falls back to repeat-last when its recent error is high. Leak-tested.
app.node.network.role: Scores every cell, picks 4 beams and splits 100 W. Proposes only; it cannot execute.
app.node.fallback.role: Takes over when the Network agent crashes, returns malformed output or times out. No model, no forecast.
app.node.kb.role: Evidence is retrieved once at start-up, so reading documents never slows a decision. Quotes must be verbatim.
app.node.policy.role: Checks the proposal against operating constraints and returns verdicts with citations. Fails closed if unavailable.
app.node.profile.role: Cap, emergency exemption, escalation and fail-safe values for one context. Changing it never touches the model.
app.node.safety.role: Requires emergency cells to be lit when their data starts to age. Watches starvation and power concentration.
app.node.supervisor.role: Detects and types conflicts, applies fallbacks and resolves by fixed precedence: limits > constraints > safety > optimisation.
app.node.guard.role: Enforces beam count, power budget, floors, signalling deadlines and caps. Raw model output never reaches the network.
app.node.audit.role: Records what was proposed, what ran, conflicts and sources. Conflicts and failures go to a human review queue.
app.node.twin.role: Queues, interference-aware SINR and KPIs. Simulation only: nothing here touches a real satellite.
app.flood.lede: Press play. Each agent sees only its part of a simulated flood.
app.flood.demand_sub: Bar: demand now. Tick: what the forecast expects. Glow: beam on it.
app.legend.rest: warmer = more backlog · select a cell to chart it
app.flood.approved: Proposal approved; no agent raised an issue.
app.flood.agents_more: What each agent knew at this moment
app.flood.audit_more: See the audit record for this moment
app.agent.network.role: Telemetry, forecast. Maximises KPIs with BRIDGE.
app.agent.safety.role: Emergency declarations, KPIs. Protects priority traffic.
app.agent.supervisor.role: Sees all. Hard limits > constraints > safety > optimisation.
app.flood.blind_one: Not told about {n} event already released.
app.flood.blind_many: Not told about {n} events already released.
app.flood.no_exemption: The search for an emergency exemption from a power limit found nothing in the corpus.
app.flood.chart_power_sub: Watts per slot. The marker is the {w} W cap on border cells from slot 50.
app.flood.insight: Across this replay the Policy agent trimmed {n} proposals and no limit was broken. Emergency cells are given a beam whenever their data starts to age, not in every slot, which keeps the other areas served.
app.stress.more: See a deliberate safety test: what happens if the AI proposes 50 W?
app.stress.h4: Injected on purpose, not part of the flood above
app.stress.p: A script forces a 50 W proposal on cell 13 at slot {s}. Limit: {cap} W (a test limit). Executed: {w} W, with the remainder moved to other beams and a human review raised.
app.stress.natural: Would BRIDGE do this unprompted? Across {n} decisions in all traffic types, {p} proposed 50 W or more on one beam (largest {m} W). It is rare, which is why the check must stay.
app.ev.h2: Fewer missed deadlines in every test. Under heavy load, it trades speed for them.
app.ev.lede: Same {n} unseen test situations for every strategy; OrbitFlow averaged over {s} trained models.
app.ev.choose: Choose one test group and one result to compare.
app.ev.ci: Each point is an average; its line shows the 95% confidence interval.
app.ev.stats: OrbitFlow vs simple scheduler, same {n} situations: difference {d} (95% CI {lo} to {hi}), {w} better, {l} worse, {ties} tied. Wilcoxon signed-rank, Holm-corrected p {p}; effect size {e}.
app.ev.deeper: Explore stress tests, agent trade-offs, and what each AI component adds
app.ev.harder_sub: Same comparison under tougher conditions. Green line: OrbitFlow better. Orange line: simple scheduler better.
app.ev.harder_insight: Late data falls in every row. Average delay is the catch: when capacity gets scarce, OrbitFlow protects deadlines at the cost of a longer average wait.
app.ev.cost_sub: Flood scenario, {n} runs. “Agents” includes need-based emergency service.
app.ev.cost_note: Need-based emergency service delivers less emergency data than serving emergency cells in every slot ({a} vs {b}), with no emergency deadline missed in either, and about the same as no agents ({c} without vs {e} with). The agents’ gain is keeping to the limit.
app.ev.parts: What each part of the AI adds
app.ev.parts_note: Reinforcement learning halves the delay of the rule it started from. The forecast cuts delay further, with little change in late data. Training from scratch also reached low delay on validation ({a} ms vs {b} ms), so copying the rule is a useful start but not essential.
app.ev.sens_more: See the full methods and engineering sensitivity
app.ev.sens_sub: Same trained AI, one radio parameter changed at a time, {n} runs each.
app.ev.sens_note: Episodes per condition: {a} (scenarios, passes), {b} (others). Seeds from {s}. Full statistics are in results/multirun.json and docs/REPORT.md.
app.lab.h2: Tighten the limit. Worsen the storm. See which one hurts.
app.lab.lede: Each square is a complete, precomputed run.
app.lab.cap: Test power limit near the border:
app.lab.heat_note: Brighter is better. ⚑ marks a run with a human-review referral.
app.lab.s_review: The supervisor referred this case to a human. Emergency cells received {p} of arrivals.
app.lab.s_fade: Emergency service drops to {p} without a sustained shortfall alarm: capacity dips intermittently. Fade is the cause; loosening the cap barely changes it.
app.lab.s_breach: Without agents, BRIDGE would breach this cap in {n} slots.
app.lab.s_loose: This cap is loose enough that BRIDGE never reaches it.
app.lab.chart_note: Data waiting in the surge area, cell {c}. Precomputed run
app.lab.live_more: Run a fresh simulation with custom settings
app.lab.pfd_more: How antenna limits and rain affect the result
app.lab.pfd: Using the ITU-R SF.358-5 limit as a guide
app.lab.pfd_sub: Regulators limit power reaching the ground, not watts per beam. This turns that limit into a cap for each area and moment, across a range of antenna gains. {n} runs each.
app.lab.pfd_insight: A loose limit barely matters, which is what the grid above shows. A tight one can dominate: at 30 dBi, emergency service falls to {p}. Antenna gain decides which world you are in.
app.lab.fact_more: See why, and how rain and limits combine
app.lab.fact: Rain × power limit, {n} paired runs per cell
app.lab.fact_note: The effects compound: at 12 dB and 8 W, the combined loss is {p} points beyond the sum of each alone. A 22 W limit rarely hurts because signal quality is capped by interference between beams: going from 25 W to 22 W moves that ceiling only from {a} to {b} dB, and capacity grows only with the logarithm of it.
app.game.h2: You be the satellite. Can you beat the AI?
app.game.lede: Pick four areas to light. Keep the people waiting served, and watch for the flood. Your choices run through the same simulator as OrbitFlow, slowed {n} times so a human can play.
app.game.tap: Tap an area to give it a beam. Picking a fifth drops your oldest.
app.game.win: You beat the AI. Seriously impressive.
app.game.draw: A draw. You held your own.
app.game.note: You saw exact backlogs and decided at human speed. OrbitFlow used data one slot old, set the power on each beam, and decided in about 1 ms. It also had to reach every area for signalling, a duty your game skips.
